Genesis

The Beginning

Introduction

The meaning of the word Hinisis, (is) “beginning”. This document (LIT reading), here is written the making of the sky/heaven and earth/ground, the origin of people, and the beginning of sin and suffering here in the world. Also written here is the story about the people chosen by God (MS Manama) and his bringing them to the place he promised to them.

This document (LIT reading) is divided into two:

1/ The making of the world and the story about people. Here can be read the story about Adan and Iba, about Kain and Abil, and about Nuwi and the flooding of the water, and about the high house/building in Babil.

2/ The story about the first elders of the Israilitas. Abraham was the first elder of the Israilitas who became famous for his believing and trusting and his obeying the command of God. The story about his child Isaak also follows, and his grandchild Hakub (also called Israil), and the twelve (12) children of Hakub who (are) the origin of the twelve (12) descendants of Israil. It's also storied here about Husi the child of Hakub and what happened to him that was the reason that Hakub went to Ihiptu with his children.

We(incl) can also read here the story about various people who had_descendants on the top of the ground and became_nations (LIT made_nations). Above all, it's storied here the great work of God who made the heaven/sky and earth and everything in it.

At the end of the story, it's storied the unending promise of God to his people. God won't forget his promise and he doesn't ignore his people because he teaches them and helps (them). And he is the (one who) judges and punishes all who do evil.

What's written(pl) in this document (LIT reading)

The making of God of the sky/heaven and the world \ior 1:1–2:25\ior*

The beginning of sin and suffering \ior 3:1‑24\ior*

The story from Adan to Noah \ior 4:1–5:32\ior*

Nuwi and the flooding of the river \ior 6:1–10:32\ior*

The high building in Babil \ior 11:1‑9\ior*

The story from Sim to Abraham \ior 11:10‑32\ior*

The elders of the Hibruwanons: Abraham, Isaak, and Hakub \ior 12:1–35:29\ior*

The descendants of Isaw \ior 36:1‑43\ior*

Husi and his brothers/siblings \ior 37:1–45:28\ior*

The Hibruwanon in Ihiptu \ior 46:1–50:26\ior*
